## Backing Query SQL

```sql
SELECT
  _stage_inner."orders.order_date" AS "order_date",
  _stage_inner."orders.rev" AS "rev"
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date) AS "orders.order_date",
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
  FROM orders AS orders
  GROUP BY
    DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date)
) AS _stage_inner
```

## Data Profile SQL

```sql
WITH monthly_rev AS (
  SELECT
    _stage_inner."orders.order_date" AS "order_date",
    _stage_inner."orders.rev" AS "rev"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date) AS "orders.order_date",
      CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
    FROM orders AS orders
    GROUP BY
      DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date)
  ) AS _stage_inner
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS "monthly_rev._count",
  COUNT(DISTINCT monthly_rev.order_date) AS "monthly_rev.order_date_count_distinct",
  CAST(AVG(monthly_rev.rev) AS DOUBLE) AS "monthly_rev.rev_avg"
FROM monthly_rev AS monthly_rev
LIMIT 3
```

args.message: I can't give a daily breakdown from monthly_rev. That model stores one row per month: order_date is already rounded down to the first of the month, and rev is the total for the whole month. Once the data is summed by month, the daily amounts can't be recovered. When I asked it for day-level results, the query engine refused because the column is only available by month. For January 2025, monthly_rev can only give the single month total. The underlying orders table (order_date, amount) does have daily detail, so a day-by-day breakdown would have to be built from orders instead.
